words.row_comment: Algorithm enable flags word 15 (EEPROM 0x1a8; e2m 106B +20 LAMP_CON / AUX_DRVR): the client feedback override enables of the 16 discrete driver outputs - bit n overrides output n's read-back. Low byte = lamp port read-back 0xFFD005 (outputs 0-7), high byte = driver port read-back 0xFFD007 (outputs 8-15). mc68k_sampleAndDebounceDiscreteInputs (0x80bcd2 / 0x80bcd3) and mc68k_ioDriverStrobeHandler (0x80bd02 / auxiliary_driver_feedback_bits) apply discrete_input_override_mask_ptr[5] (bits 0-7) and [4] (bits 8-15) as read-back & ~mask | value & mask with the values 0x80bcdc / 0x80bcdd; cm550_FUN_000206a8 tests bits 0 and 1 by index (table bits 240 / 241). 0x1 wait to start lamp, 0x2 stop engine lamp, 0x4 water in fuel lamp, 0x8 no record, 0x10 engine protection lamp, 0x20 solenoid A, 0x40 warning lamp, 0x80 fuel shutoff (FSO / VP44 pump enable), 0x100 engine brake relay (RLY1), 0x200 / 0x400 cold start aid relays 1 / 2 (RLY2 / RLY3), 0x800 relay 7 (A/C clutch), 0x1000 relay 5 (prime pump), 0x2000 relay 6 (ether start), 0x4000 relay 4, 0x8000 fan clutch (SOL1). Plain word: nothing reads it by its own address so a bitfield would render nowhere. Dump 0x0000. (no row before; PR #53 round 92)
words.code_tests: No reference to 0x803cb2 / 0x803cb3 in the dumped 256 KB ROM. Byte masks through discrete_input_override_mask_ptr (= &switch_override_configuration 0x803cae; set by cm550_initializeDiscreteInputs): [5] = 0x803cb3 (bits 0-7) and [4] = 0x803cb2 (bits 8-15) in mc68k_sampleAndDebounceDiscreteInputs and mc68k_ioDriverStrobeHandler. Indexed single-bit tests on base 0x803c94: cm550_FUN_000206a8(0x20, 0) and (0x21, 6), called from cm550_FUN_00021070, test table bits 0xd0 + 0x20 = 240 (bit 0) and 241 (bit 1).
words.writes: none (no store / bset / bclr / ori / andi on the address; only the generic EEPROM mirror and tool memory writers)
words.differences_from_cm848: CM848 has no row, no e2m record (none of the 23 CHR e2m files has 106B +0020) and no reader; no CM848 counterpart.

words.differences_from_cm848: Bits 0 2 3 6 8 9 11-15 match CM848's algorithm_enable_flags_18_t (field names reused) and bit 10 is reserved in both. CM550 names bits 1 (WPEAFG engine warmup protection), 4 (TRAGEN trending) and 5 (UDEN datalogger), each code-tested and set in the dump, where CM848 has reserved_bit_1 / 4 / 5 (no CHR record and no CM848 reader). CM848 names bit 7 executive_timing_enable (CHR SSECTMEA, read by its executive frame interrupt handler); CM550 has no record or reader for it. So the type is cm550_algorithm_enable_flags_18_t, not shared. CM848 also reads bits 8 and 14, which CM550 does not.

proposal.notes:
Batch W3 covers CM550 e2m 106B words 15 16 17 18 19 22 23 (0x803cb2-0x803cc3, EEPROM 0x1a8-0x1b9). Every ROM reference is a move.w read, so none of the seven words is written.

TYPES: words 16 and 18 become cm550_ bitfields, because they have direct single-bit andi.w / andi.l tests and no writes. Words 15 17 19 22 23 stay plain words, following CM848's precedent: it keeps words 0 / 7 / 8 / 26 as words when nothing tests them through their own address.
- Words 15 and 17 are read only as byte masks through discrete_input_override_mask_ptr (= &switch_override_configuration 0x803cae: [4]/[5] = word 15 high/low, [9] = word 17 low), plus indexed bit tests through word 0's base.
- Word 19 has no reference anywhere in the dumped 256 KB ROM. Code above 0x40000 is not dumped, so 'no reader' is limited to the dump. The EEPROM holds 0x00c0 there.
- Words 22 and 23 are loaded whole into d4 and tested with a variable channel mask, so a bitfield would print as a piece.
Fields are still listed for the plain words so they can go into the row comments.

LOGICAL INPUT RULE (also covers words 13 and 14, outside this batch): logical input k has
- status byte 0x80bcce + k/8, bit k%8 (e2m 000E + k/8)
- user value 0x80bcd8 + k/8 (000E +0xA + k/8)
- priority 0x80bd4a + k (e2m 12A8 + k)
- enable = table bit 208 + k = word 13 + k/16, bit k%16. On this big-endian CPU the mask byte for inputs 8j..8j+7 is 0x803cae + 2*(j/2) + (1 - j%2).
cm550_FUN_00020890 uses the rule for the 17-entry j1939_input_signal_descriptor_table (ROM 0x20108). Logical inputs: 72 9 54 11 10 3 1 2 14 13 60 56 58 20 19 15 54. cm550_FUN_000206a8(k, j) is called with (0x36,1) (0x36,4) (0x21,6) (0x20,0) (0x36,2). Words 15-17 map as follows:
- word 15 = output read-back overrides (bit n = output n; lamp port 0xFFD005 / driver port 0xFFD007)
- word 16 = decoded cruise byte 0x80bcd4 and power take-off byte 0x80bcd5
- word 17 = torque derate byte 0x80bcd6 and A/C pressure byte 0x80bcd7

WHERE THE E2M DISAGREES WITH THE CODE:
- Word 16, power take-off resume: the code uses bit 8 (andi #0x100 at 0x153fc with value 0x80bcdf bit 0; J1939 entry 11 = logical input 56; 12A8 +38 DSPZPTRU). The 106B record DSPTRUUO's 0x2000 is wrong for this build, so bit 13 is reserved.
- Word 16 bit 6 is the auxiliary shutdown, per DSAUSHUO 0x40 and J1939 entry 2. However, the e2m's own value, status and priority records sit at logical input 62 (bit 14). J1939 entry 16 (engine derate switch) also points at 54; the torque derate's own slot is 64 = word 17 bit 0, so entry 16 looks like a firmware table quirk.
- Word 17 bit 8 has no e2m enable record; only the code (J1939 entry 0) names it.
- Word 15: the 0x800 / 0x4000 records say BIT 14 / BIT 11. The masks are the correct ones, because they line up with the value byte E +F and the status byte E +35. Where the two record sets name a bit differently (87 functional names vs 88 RLYn / LAMPn names), the field names use the functional names this CSV already uses and keep the RLYn / LAMPn mnemonic in the comment.
- Column 15 of the e2m (8700199999 vs 8800199999) looks like a YYDDD start date followed by 99999. It does not select a variant, so it cannot settle these conflicts; the code does.

CM848: no field renames. None of the 23 CHR e2m files has a 106B +0026 record at 0x2 / 0x10 / 0x20 or a +0028 record at 0x4 / 0x10, and the CM848 .cpp renders none of those reserved bits. CM848 also has no row and no record for words 15 16 17 22 23. Word 18 is not shared: CM550 adds bits 1 / 4 / 5 and lacks CM848's bit 7 executive_timing_enable.
